specialRules.ruleFull: Dwarfs are taken out of action only on a 6 on the Injury chart: 1-2 is knocked down, 3-5 stunned and 6 out of action.
Dwarfs ignore the special rules of clubs, maces and the like.
Dwarfs never suffer movement penalties for wearing armour.
All Dwarfs hate Orcs and Goblins.
The warband may never include an Elven Hired Sword or Dramatis Persona of any kind.

A Dwarf Hero taken out of action in either of the ways below is so shamed that he becomes a Trollslayer. He loses any special ability, Leader among them, but keeps his skills; he is immune to psychology, and he may learn the Troll Slayer special skills from the rulebook. Except for the leader, his place may be taken by another Dwarf at the next recruiting phase; if the leader becomes a Trollslayer, choose another leader as if he had died.

Taken out of action in the Dwarf player's first or second turn.

Taken out of action in single combat by an opponent with Weapon Skill 2 or Strength 2, or by an animal.
Up to 3 man-sized models (no ogres and the like) may be placed anywhere on the table at the end of the first turn, no closer than 8" to any enemy model.
While a Dwarf Weaponsmith or a Master Craftsman is in the warband, every missile weapon of the warband has 6" added to its range.

A Dwarf Brewer brings a barrel of his finest brew to each battle, and the leader lets D3 of his Heroes drink before the battle. Only Dwarfs may drink it. Name the models who drink, then roll a D6 for each:

D6 | Brew
1-2 | XXXXXX: the warrior is immune to fear for the rest of the battle.
3-4 | Troll Brew: the warrior is subject to frenzy for the rest of the battle.
5-6 | Special Brew: the warrior's Weapon Skill and Strength are each +1 for the rest of the battle. This may take him above his racial maximum, but never above 10.
Any model in the warband within 6" of the Dwarf Master Craftsman may use his Leadership instead of his own.

flags.what: The warband's minimum of 3 models is not imported: our templates hold no minimum.

The PDF prints no equipment lists of its own: "All of the equipment lists from Town Crier 6 (or Best of Town Crier) apply". The Dwarf Warrior and Thunderer lists are taken from our own Dwarf Treasure Hunters warband, which is that list, not from any other PDF. The fighters' entries name the "Dwarf Thunderers" and "Dwarf Warriors" lists.

"All of the special rules from Town Crier 6 apply apart from Incomparable Miners": Hard to Kill, Hard Head, Armour, Hate Orcs and Goblins and Grudgebearers are carried over from our own Dwarf Treasure Hunters warband in our words, and Incomparable Miners is left out.

"Dwarf Heroes may use any of the Dwarf Special Skills listed in Town Crier 6": the Special column names our Dwarves skill group (Master of Blades, Extra Tough, Resource Hunter, True Grit, Thick Skull), so the warband declares no group of its own.
The Dwarf Axe ("as detailed in Town Crier 6") is our Dwarf Axe, on the Dwarf Warrior list at 15 gc.
The Shame rule is kept as a warband rule: it turns a Hero into a Trollslayer, which the app cannot do to a unit.
The Engineers rule names a "Dwarf Weaponsmith", which is the Engineers' Guild name for the Expert Craftsman (p27); it is kept as printed.
The Expert Craftsman's Weapons/Armour line says "A Dwarf Master Craftsman may be equipped...", read as the Expert Craftsman's own entry; both use the Thunderer list.
The alternative Guild names (Principal Hewer, Chief Engineer, Master Brewer and the rest) are not imported: they are names a player may use, not fighters of their own.
Henchmen are bought in groups of 1-5, which is every Henchman group's size here.
No Henchman maximum is printed for Artisans or Labourers; the Thunderers are 0-5.
